about: MUTATING — merge the public mirror's approved pull request BY MACHINE, as the GitHub App: the `merge` step of publish-to-github (backlog 602fe95f, David 2026-09-30: option (ii), "NOBODY pushes or merges main by hand"; after David's passkey approval of the daily publish, the GitHub App merges the publish PR, authored and committed as David Auld <david@algedonic.dev>, and main is protected so only the App can update it). Runs infra/forge/publish-github-pr.sh with --merge FIXED IN THE ARGV and no packet-supplied input — jobs.spawn carries no args list, so a rule that files this can file a merge and nothing else. The dispatcher rule merge-publish-pr-on-merge-ready files it when the publish packet's `merge` step goes ready: the PR's check reading was green, or its judgement found nothing real. The run reads its own request's metadata.for_publish — the packet whose merge went ready, never the first open one (backlog 16a9c5ae) — requires that packet's merge step ready and, before any token or push: re-reads the APPROVAL exactly as a publish does — the live passkey stamp by an approver this verb's sibling file infra/ops/verbs/publish-github-pr.json names, bound to the approve step's current shape, over source_sha = scanned_sha = what measure recorded, with a clean scan re-run here over that tree — because the passkey signed the TREE and the merge lands exactly that tree, so no second prompt is asked for; reads what open-pr recorded (pr_url on the mirror, snapshot_commit, head on the mirror's own publish/<date>-<snapshot> branch, the same source_sha); fetches that branch anonymously and requires it to hold the snapshot, whose tree is the approved commit's tree, whose one parent is the mirror's main as it stands now, and whose author and committer are the `publisher` publish-github-pr.json declares; asks GitHub (anonymously) for the PR — open, from the mirror's own branch into main, head the snapshot, opened by the App: the bot login and id open-pr recorded from GitHub's own answer when the App opened it, never any Bot — for the rules main carries, refusing when no required status check is named (the ruleset defines green, and until github-set-branch-protection has applied it nothing is merged) or one is not pinned to an App (a check any App can post defines no green), and for the head's check-runs, refusing while any run of a required check has not completed and unless the newest of that App's runs completed `success`. Then it renders the one-hour App installation token the broker minted for THIS request (rule broker-mints-the-algedonic-dev-publish-token-when-a-publish-request-is-filed, v2) and FAST-FORWARDS main to the snapshot with a plain, never-forced push: the commit on main is the approved commit byte for byte, authored and committed as the publisher — a squash or a merge commit would be a new commit GitHub mints with an identity the API does not let the caller choose. Proof: git ls-remote reads main at the snapshot, and GitHub reads the PR merged (it marks a PR merged when its head reaches the base). It revokes the token, writes pr_state onto the packet (the key the publish region reads), completes `merge` with merged_sha, and ends `publish-github-pr: merged <pr url> — main reads <sha>`. Idempotent: a re-run after main already reads the snapshot pushes nothing and re-proves. One run at a time: it holds the publish lock. Every refusal names what failed and exits non-zero, and complete-publish-merge-step-on-merge-publish-pr-answered annotates the step and files an urgent alert. The exit says whether main moved (backlog 16a9c5ae; review af3f2996), decided by READING the mirror's main as soon as the packet is known — fetched, and asked whether it is or CONTAINS open-pr's snapshot (review 89d4d390; a --merge run that dies before that read exits 4): 2 (refused) or 1 (failed) only after the snapshot was read provably NOT on main and before a push — nothing was merged, and the protocol closes the packet at merge-refused so the next daily publish runs and supersedes the PR; 3, from the moment main reads the snapshot (found there, pushed, or a push that errored but landed, read back), leaves the packet open and troubled until a request for it proves the merge again, without the publish branch; 4 before main was read. Any exit the run did not choose is held to its state's own, and every system-of-record write after the push is bounded. Authorized by David 2026-09-30 on backlog 602fe95f.
